references.text: Describes the same event where the Lord led the Israelites out of Egypt.
The Egyptians pursued the Israelites with chariots and horsemen to the Sea of Reeds.
The Egyptians pursued the Israelites into the middle of the sea with horses, chariots, and horsemen.
The sea rolled back over the Egyptian army with its chariots and horsemen.
Moses' song describes how Pharaoh's chariots and army were cast into the sea.
Moses reminds the people of how the Lord let the Sea of Reeds overwhelm the Egyptian army with horses and chariots.
Nehemiah recounts how God saw the distress of their ancestors in Egypt and at the Sea of Reeds, and parted the sea for them.
The psalm describes how God split the sea and led the people through it.
The psalm tells how God rebuked the Sea of Reeds and led the people through, while the enemies were overwhelmed by the water.
The psalm praises God for parting the Sea of Reeds and leading Israel through, while Pharaoh and his army were cast into the sea.
Hebrews mentions that the Israelites passed through the Red Sea in faith, while the Egyptians drowned when they attempted to do the same.
